title: 🤝 The Interview — Théo Ch.2
ps_sub: Théo's Internship Adventure · Ch.2 The Interview · A2–B1 · self-marking
foot: 🤝 BAC PRO 1 · Théo's Internship Adventure · Ch.2 The Interview — self-marking 🤝
story: Good news! A recruiter has just phoned Théo: the company wants to meet him for an interview on Friday. Théo is excited but nervous. He has never had a real job interview before.

First, he researches the company online. The firm has grown a lot since 2010, and last year it opened a new hub near the highway. Its trucks are used all over Europe, and thousands of packages are sent every day. Théo takes notes to remember the key facts.
Then he prepares for the big day. He chooses smart clothes for the interview and prints his CV to show his skills. His teacher says: "You should research the company, and you mustn't be late!"
On Friday, Théo is interviewed by the manager. Here is part of their conversation:

Manager: "Why do you want this internship?"
Théo: "I want it because your warehouse is very modern."
Manager: "What are your strengths?"
Théo: "I am organized and I work hard."
Manager: "When can you start?"
Théo: "I can start in June."
Manager: "Great! We are happy to offer you the job."
Théo: "Thank you very much!"
The manager was happy with his answers — and Théo is hired! 🎉

sections.name: TR Traduction
sections.heading: Traduis : present perfect ou prétérit ?
sections.instr: Lis la phrase française et choisis la bonne traduction anglaise. Le repère de temps te dit quel temps utiliser.

items.text: « Hier, Théo a passé son entretien. » ___
options: Yesterday, Théo has had his interview.

items.text: « Il porte toujours une cravate à l'entretien. » ___
options: He always wears a tie to an interview.
He always wore a tie to an interview.
items.answer: He always wears a tie to an interview.

items.text: « L'entreprise a ouvert un bureau à Lyon en 2020. » ___
options: The company opened an office in Lyon in 2020.
The company has opened an office in Lyon in 2020.
items.answer: The company opened an office in Lyon in 2020.

items.text: « Elle dirige l'équipe depuis cinq ans. » ___
options: She managed the team for five years.
She has managed the team for five years.
items.answer: She has managed the team for five years.

items.text: « Le manager a déjà lu son CV. » ___
options: The manager has already read his CV.
The manager already read his CV.
items.answer: The manager has already read his CV.

items.text: « La semaine dernière, ils ont embauché deux stagiaires. » ___
options: Last week, they hired two trainees.
Last week, they have hired two trainees.
items.answer: Last week, they hired two trainees.

items.text: « As-tu déjà négocié un salaire ? » ___
options: Did you ever negotiate a salary?
Have you ever negotiated a salary?
items.answer: Have you ever negotiated a salary?

items.text: « Il n'a pas encore reçu de réponse. » ___
options: He didn't receive an answer yet.
He hasn't received an answer yet.
items.answer: He hasn't received an answer yet.

sections.name: FT For/To
sections.heading: FOR or TO?
sections.instr: « pour » se traduit par TO + verbe (le but) ou par FOR + nom. Choisis le bon mot.

sections.name: PV Passive
sections.heading: The passive voice
sections.instr: Qui fait l'action n'est pas important : on utilise la voix passive (be + participe passé).

sections.name: MOD Modals
sections.heading: Interview advice (modals)
sections.instr: Conseil, obligation, interdiction ou pas nécessaire ? Choisis le modal qui a le bon sens.

items.text: It's a good idea: you ___ research the company before the interview.
It is strictly forbidden: you ___ be late — arrive early!
It's a rule: you ___ bring your ID card to enter the building.
Never do this in an interview: you ___ lie about your skills.
The dress code is relaxed, so you ___ wear a tie.
It's obligatory: you ___ turn off your phone during the interview.
It's only advice: you ___ speak too fast.
It's optional: at the end, you ___ ask a few questions if you want.

sections.name: RS Reported
sections.heading: Reported speech (said / told)
sections.instr: On rapporte ce qui a été dit à l'entretien. Attention : say / tell (+ personne), et le temps recule (want → wanted).
